messages:
maria (infra): Quick sync — want to land a compact Grafana 'regional GPU scorecard' panel that summarizes GPU health and a short decision-rule runbook for ECC/Xid/flaky cards. Current dashboards are noisy and per-cluster. Trying to push a single-row view for operations and an auto-flagging rule.
Tom K: SGTM. What metrics do you want in the one-liner? availability, ECC count, Xid spikes, drain rate?
maria (infra): Exactly. Proposal: compute a weighted health score per region: 50% availability (node up pct), 25% ECC errors normalized per 1e6 ops, 15% Xid spike indicator (binary per-window), 10% recent drain/replacement rate. Score 0-100 where <70 is degraded. Thoughts?
Sanjay R: I like weights. Suggest also a ‘flaky card’ signal: number of nodes with >1 kernel reset in 24h. That should bump the severity. Maybe reduce Xid weight to 10 and flaky to 15.
Lia (oncall): +1 to flaky card signal. Also we need actionable alert thresholds that map to runbook steps: 70->investigate, 50->suppress scheduling & plan drain, 30->force replacement and limit capacity to avoid noisy neighbor impact.
maria (infra): Updated weights: availability 50, ECC 20, flaky 15, Xid 10, drain-rate 5. Will prototype.
infra-bot: New panel draft uploaded: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/xyz123/regional-gpu-scorecard (permission: infra, oncall)
Tom K: Nice. Can we implement the core queries as PromQL? Here's a starter for ECC normalized:

```
sum by(region) (rate(node_gpu_ecc_errors_total[1h]))
/
sum by(region) (rate(node_gpu_compute_cycles_total[1h]))
* 1e6
```

Map that into a 0-100 scaled value by taking a percentile baseline and inverting.
Sanjay R: For Xid spikes I'd prefer a change-rate detector rather than absolute count. Something like:

```
increase(nvml_xid_errors_total[10m]) > 5
```

Then convert to 1 if true else 0 per region and multiply by weight.
maria (infra): Agreed. For flaky card we can use kernel resets metric + daily unique node count:

```
sum by(region) (increase(nvml_kernel_reset_total[24h]) > 1)
```

Then normalize by total nodes per region.
Lia (oncall): For alerts, can we tie the 70/50/30 buckets to a single stat panel and a Prometheus rule that emits 'region_gpu_health_status{severity="investigate|moderate|critical"}'? That makes routing easier.
Tom K: Yes. Example transform: compute score then use recording rule to set severity threshold labels. Pseudocode rule:

```
- record: region:gpu_health_score:avg
  expr: <compute weighted score per region>

- alert: RegionGPUDegraded
  expr: region:gpu_health_score:avg < 70
  labels:
    severity: 'investigate'
```

Then additional alerts for <50 and <30 with escalating severity.
maria (infra): Also want the Grafana panel to show the top 3 contributing signals per-region (so on-call sees why it dropped). We can add a table transform that lists signal contributions.
Sanjay R: Will add a `topk(3, ...)` style helper that returns signal names and relative weights. Also include a small sparkline for Xid over last 6h.
Lia (oncall): Runbook notes: 1) check node driver/kernel mismatch, 2) query recent kernel reset logs, 3) cordon & drain if >=2 nodes affected in region, 4) escalate to HW replace if errors persist after swap. Put a link in alert: https://confluence.redwood.ai/gpu-runbook
maria (infra): Thanks. I'll wire recording rules + alerting and push the panel. Will tag you for review @TomK @SanjayR. infra-bot, leave a deploy note when rules are applied.
infra-bot: Recording rules applied to prometheus-prod at 2026-03-18T15:22:30Z. :white_check_mark:
Tom K: Quick nit — pick a conservative baseline for ECC scaling to avoid false positives from occasional single-bit ECC bursts. Use 95th percentile of last 30d as baseline.
maria (infra): Good call. I'll use pct_95 as baseline and floor contribution to 0 for tiny regions with <4 GPUs.
Lia (oncall): One more ask: add per-region capacity impact estimate: e.g., 'estimated available vGPU slots' so SRE can plan fallbacks. Small column in panel.
maria (infra): Will add. I'll post the final JSON dashboard and the prometheus rule file here when ready.
Tom K: :thumbsup:"
